verdicts.reason: I could not refute it. Skin:PaintAce looks up the painter with lib.__acePaint[rawget(widget,'type')] (SkinAce.lua:673), and the durability repaint hooks such as SetDisabled do the same lookup (SkinAce.lua:258). AuraMaster's constructor sets w.type = 'AuraMasterDropdown' (settings/OptionsSetup.lua:77) on purpose, so the widget goes back to AuraMaster's own pool and not the shared one. Schema rows reach that type through row.dialogControl, which the library's makeDropdown passes straight to AceGUI:Create (OptionsWidgets.lua:779-783). The library's own paint of those rows therefore returns false. Every workaround I tried fails. (a) Flipping widget.type to 'Dropdown' around a PaintAce call writes to the widget table and is overridden at every SetDisabled repaint. (b) Painting the widget's frame with the vocabulary's S.Dropdown, S.Text or S.Panel leaves a pooled AceGUI widget with no restore: lib:Untrack (Skin.lua:707) forgets the frame but does not unpaint it. It also skips the shared AceGUI pullout hook that PAINT.Dropdown installs, and under eui it would hand a pooled object to EllesmereUI, which §5 forbids. #107 names both of these. (c) Retiring the type (the inventory's D11) brings back the cross-addon LEFT-justification leak, because the library's makers give the host no hook after Create, so it cannot chain a Skin:OnRelease restore onto schema rows. What is missing: a way for PaintAce, its repaint hook and its restore to treat a host-registered type as a stock type, such as Skin:AliasAceType(hostType,'Dropdown') or a rawget-read widget.paintAs. With that, Ka0s Default draws exactly what PAINT.Dropdown draws today.

verdicts.reason: No token in the SkinDefs schema holds {1, 0.91, 0.55} in Ka0s Default. The plan says the run must stop and ask before any change to Ka0s Default's look. No primitive can shift a token's value either: S.Text, S.Color and P.tint apply a token as it is, and the library's blend/FOLLOW/ACCENT_WASH derivations are internal to SkinDefs and not exposed to addons. Doing the arithmetic in the addon would be a hard-coded literal, which is anti-pattern #107. Rung 4 (game-meaning colors) does not cover it: the pale gold is BankLedger's own design choice (LedgerTable.lua:32-35 calls it deliberately lighter than the heading gold), not a client color like quality or class. So rung 2 applies: a new token sem.goldAlt, Ka0s Default {1,0.91,0.55,1}, FOLLOW sem.gold. This follows the LK-A3 *Alt precedent. Only Ka0s Default sets sem.gold, and the eui source keeps Ka0s Default's value, so every skin resolves to a light gold that stays legible on the GameTooltip title line too. The name and description in the claim are sound.

The claim rests on two premises, and both are wrong. (1) skinning.md:81 says only that 'Lines the addon writes onto GameTooltip take their colors from the skin'. It does not require gtip.* tokens, and no rule in skinning.md or in anti-pattern #107 names the gtip family. Any token read meets the rule. (2) text.value is not darkened by any skin. In SkinDefs.lua only Ka0s Default ({0.8,0.8,0.82,1}, line 230) and High Contrast (#E0E0E0, line 732, which is lighter) set it. Obsidian, Azeroth (now dark leather, not parchment; it does not set text.value), Glass, Ember, WoW Default, Midnight and Forever all inherit Ka0s Default's value. SkinEUI's derive() changes only the ACCENT/PANEL/FLAT/FONT token lists, so eui keeps Ka0s Default's text.value too. text.value is therefore exactly W.MUTED today and stays legible on Blizzard's dark tooltip under all nine skins and eui. Button's hover (:120) recolors the label and does not paint a fill. Stacking two washes does not reach 0.25: list.hover plus menu.hover gives 1-0.9*0.85 = 0.235, and list.hover plus tab.rule gives 0.244. Reading S.Color('text.accent') or btn.hover and then calling SetColorTexture(r,g,b,0.25) types an alpha at the call site, which anti-pattern #107 names. LootHistory's 0.95 literals are on data bars, not chrome, so they do not set a precedent here. The cheapest rung-2 fix is one ACCENT_WASH entry, ('btn.iconHover', 0.25). With it every skin and eui derives the token from its accent, and Ka0s Default stays {1,0.82,0,0.25}. The hover is reachable: the remove button (Category.lua:611) uses this widget.

No token holds {1,0x88/255,0}. The nearest are sem.warn, text.link and q.legendary, all {1,0.5,0}, which writes the escape as ff8000. That differs from the ff8800 drawn today by 8/255 on green. Other near values are sem.boundWarbandUE {0.95,0.52,0.12}, series[2] {0.95,0.55,0.15} and strip.test {1,0.65,0.15}. Under the run's rule (00_PLAN: the run stops to ask if Ka0s Default would change) and the SkinDefs minor-6 precedent (a new token 'where no older token held the exact value'), this is a gap. The semantically right existing token is sem.warn. Accepting it would be an owner call in DECISIONS.md: a one-byte green shift on Ka0s Default, and no new token. Either way, the escape has to come out of the L[] keys at Category.lua:709, 712, 952 and 1090 and StatPriority.lua:738. Otherwise no token read can reach it, and every locale's key changes.

verdicts.reason: Every piece already exists. Every composer passes spec.extra through appendExtra (OptionsCompose.lua:254-266): ColorPair :602, FontGroup :640, BorderGroup :676. So a host can emit its own `<key>FromSkin` bool row after the swatch without touching the composed rows' words (#106 bans only changes to labels and tooltips). The swatch tooltip can say it is not read while that row is on, through the sanctioned `tooltips` override (minor 10). Drawing goes through S.Resolve(token, stored, companion). lib:Resolve (Skin.lua:626) answers any token, colors included, when fromSkin == true. Skin.ResetToSkin already sets `<key>FromSkin = true` for a table-valued (color) key (Skin.lua:658). So R3 lands on a row the player can see and clear. verdicts.reason: I could not refute this one. S.Shell (SkinPaint.lua:925-946) takes its fill only from win.bg. It hands Core.ApplySkin shellSkin(T), whose bg is T['win.bg'], and draws win.inner at that token's own alpha (innerRule). Its only opts are noTopBar, bottomBar, noBorder and stock, so nothing can force alpha 1. No window-family token is opaque: win.bg is .92, win.bgDense .95, menu.bg .98, popup.bg .92 and tooltip.bg .95. Win.border is {0,0,0,1}, which is opaque but the wrong color. Calling NS.ApplySkin(f, Timeline.SKIN) with a table skips the facade, because Core.lua:218-227 builds S only when skin == nil. That leaves two compositions. (a) Stack an S.Shell underlay frame under the window's own S.Shell. That gives alpha 1-.08^2 = .9936 under Ka0s Default, so it is not pixel-identical to the opaque {.06,.06,.08,1}, and the inner rule then blends over a not-quite-opaque fill. In a translucent skin such as Glass the stack is still see-through, so the modal does not hide the Results window. (b) Read S.Color('win.bg') and SetColorTexture it at alpha 1, or blend win.inner by hand. Anti-pattern #107 names an alpha written at a call site, so this is a finding. S.Cover (cover.dim .6 black) changes the look as well. A rung-2 addition is needed. The proposed Shell option works, and so would a win.bgOpaque-style token. Its eui fallback is EllesmereUI's panel color at alpha 1.

S.Button's spec is BTN or BTN_PRIMARY only (SkinPaintControls.lua:131-151). Its label takes btn.text or btnPrimary.text, and the hooks on OnEnter, OnLeave, OnEnable and OnDisable re-tint it to btn(.hover/.text) or text.disabled (buttonLabel :107-118). A red label applied afterwards with S.Font(fs, r, g, b) or P.tint would therefore be overwritten on the first hover or enable. S.Text has no red role (TEXT_ROLE: body, muted, heading, headingAlt, accent, disabled, link, linkHot, title). The red hue exists as sem.statusBad {1,.32,.32}, which is exact, and sem.danger {1,1/3,1/3}. No primitive paints a box from either, and no token holds a .08-alpha red fill or a .6-alpha red edge. Composing it would need literal alphas at the call site, which #107 forbids. The shape also recurs: sem.danger was added (SkinDefs minor 5) for LootHistory's destructive menu item. A rung-2 btnDanger.* with a { danger = true } option is needed. D-2 has already accepted that the fill and edge dim differently when the button is disabled. Its rest, hover and edge values must reproduce Hud_States.lua:41 exactly.

S.Panel, S.Card, S.Inset and S.Footer each use a fixed spec (panel.*, card.*, input.*, foot.*). P.box (SkinPaint.lua:712) reads only spec tokens, and opts can only drop the bg or the border, never pick another token. The washes S.Strip and S.Cover take only strip.test {1,.65,.15,.12}, strip.sim and cover.dim. Strip.test is amber in a different hue and alpha, and it means 'test mode', not 'caution'. S.Divider(frame, { token = ... }) can fill a frame with any token, but it draws a single region and no edge. No token holds {1,.72,.29} at alpha .06, .07 or .08, or at .35 or .6. The nearest cream text token is drawer.summarySet {.91,.85,.66}, which is not the {.95,.85,.67} used today. Composing it would need literal alphas or colors (#107). The gap is real, but the proposal under-specifies Ka0s Default. Today there are three fill alphas (.06 flags, .07 hint, .08 badge), two edge alphas (.35, .6) and three creams ({.95,.85,.67}, {.95,.84,.65}, {.94,.84,.65}), plus the amber C.amber on the badge and on the flag sub-line. One callout.bg and callout.text token cannot reproduce all of them pixel-identically. Either the library carries per-variant tokens (bg, bgStrong, border, borderStrong, text, textStrong=amber), or a DECISIONS entry accepts unifying the .06, .07 and .08 fills and the three creams, which changes Ka0s Default by about .01.

I checked every sem.*, text.* and chart.* value in Ka0s Default (SkinDefs.lua:209-335) for an exact match. Ahead {.36,.86,.46} has none: sem.good is {.35,.80,.45}, sem.boundBoP {.30,.82,.42}, sem.on {.3,.85,.3} and sem.statusOk {.30,.95,.35}. Caution {1,.72,.29} has none either. The nearest is text.linkHot {1,.72,.28}, which is off by .01 in blue and means link hover, not warning, so it would break the hue-carries-meaning rule. Info {.56,.72,1} has none: sem.info is {.3,.8,1} and chart.line {.4,.6,.95}. Skinning-§4 requires meaning colors (gain and loss) to come from semantic tokens and to equal the old values under Ka0s Default. The library's own precedent (SkinDefs minor 6, LK-A3) adds a token 'where no older token held the exact value'. Red is covered by sem.statusBad. I add one caveat. Hud_Chart.lua:89-90 draws AHEAD and BEHIND at alpha .85. Reading sem.ahead or sem.statusBad and forcing .85 at the call site is a #107 alpha literal. M1 should either ship the .85 variants (for example chart.ahead and chart.behind) or record a decision on that alpha. Results_Table's blue and violet status hues are not in the list, so the inventory must still rule them as exceptions or tokens.

This one composes from what exists. The FROM_SKIN.font companion in OptionsCompose.lua:326-334 is hard-wired to hud.font, but everything that companion does uses public pieces a host can wire itself. The companion is a plain bool row named <key>FromSkin. The picker row's disabledIf field names that row. The picker row's skinValue field (OptionsWidgets W35) returns the skin's value while the bool is on. S.Resolve(owner, kind, value, fromSkin) (Skin.lua:626) accepts any token name, font.mono included. Skin.ResetToSkin (Skin.lua:650-660) sets <leaf>FromSkin wherever that key exists in the profile, not only on composer-made rows. The inventory also recommends D-15, which excludes the clocks from R3 and needs no library change at all.
verdicts.composition: Call O.FontGroup for the two clock blocks without fromSkin, or with omit = { fontFromSkin = true }. Add the companion yourself through spec.extra: { path = '<prefix>.fontFromSkin', type = 'bool', label = "Use the skin's monospace font", default = <owner's call>, startsLine = true }. On the returned font picker row, set disabledIf to that companion path and skinValue = function() return on and S.Resolve('font.mono', nil, true) or nil end. The HUD draws with S.Resolve('font.mono', profile.appearance.elapsed.font, profile.appearance.elapsed.fontFromSkin), and Skin.ResetToSkin sets the companion because the key exists. Ka0s Default's font.mono is 'JetBrains Mono' (SkinDefs.lua:206), which is today's appearance.elapsed/left.font, so the clocks are pixel-identical. Every other skin inherits or sets font.mono, and the eui source resolves it through ResolveSkin. Simpler still: take D-15 and leave the clocks out of R3.

verdicts.reason: I checked all seven values (C.TONE good .30,.85,.40; yellow 1,.96,.42; red 1,.36,.32; cyan .35,.82,.95; offspec .30,.85,.85; redMuted .72,.36,.34; bad .55,.55,.58, Constants.lua:189-207) against the whole KA0S table in SkinDefs.lua:201-370. No token holds any of them, at any alpha. The near ones (sem.good .35,.80,.45; sem.bad 1,.33,.33; sem.statusBad 1,.32,.32; sem.info .3,.8,1; sem.boundBoP .30,.82,.42; icon.dim .55,.55,.55; chart.axisAlt .55,.55,.60,.9) would all move Ka0s Default pixels. Under skinning-§4 these are meaning colors and must be read from semantic tokens. Snapping them, or adjusting them with literals at the call site, breaks either §4 or #107. Seven new sem.* tokens are needed. Note: no other skin overrides any sem.* today, apart from High Contrast's bound/unknown grays, so the proposed FOLLOW sources mostly fall back to the Ka0s constant.

strip.test is exactly {1, 0.65, 0.15, 0.12} (SkinDefs.lua:296). Its rgb is C.TONE.warn byte for byte. No other skin sets strip.test, and SkinEUI's derive (SkinEUI.lua:290-305) only overrides the accent, panel and font tokens. So its rgb is the same amber under all nine skins and eui. The proposed sem.urgent with FOLLOW from sem.warn would resolve to the same constant in every skin anyway, because FOLLOW copies only when a skin sets the source, and no skin sets sem.warn.
verdicts.composition: Text: `local r,g,b = S.Color("strip.test"); fs:SetTextColor(r,g,b)`, rgb only, the way LootHistory's NS.SkinColor drops the alpha. Bar (flat, per D5): `bar:SetColorTexture(r,g,b, <bar alpha>)`, or the same alpha DW's G1 bar path uses. The chip takes the same rgb. Ka0s Default draws 1,.65,.15 at alpha 1, exactly as today. Caveat: this borrows the test strip's amber role (skinning-§4/§7 call it a library meaning color). If the owner wants the deadline amber to retune apart from the test strip someday, sem.urgent becomes a naming change, not a pixel need.

verdicts.reason: No token holds .42,.74,.46 (sem.good .35,.80,.45; sem.boundBoEAlt .55,.80,.60; sem.boundBoP .30,.82,.42; sem.on .3,.85,.3). It is a gain/loss meaning color, so skinning-§4 requires a semantic token, and a literal or tweaked value fails #107.

There is no .92 body gray (text.body .9, text.bodyAlt .86, text.subtle .85, text.highlight 1, sem.stepReady .9,.9,.92). The one exact-rgb match is sem.boundBoE (.92,.92,.92,.95), and you could drop its alpha. But no FOLLOW ties it to body text: it stays a constant .92 gray in the dark skins and goes pure white in High Contrast. So plain table text would not follow Azeroth's, Ember's or WoW Forever's body color. That is not a reasonable composition, so text.bodyBright is needed.

Nothing is .62,.62,.64 (sem.neutral .62,.62,.66; log.count .6,.6,.62; text.muted and tab.text .7,.7,.72; gtip.muted .5; q.poor .62,.62,.62). The '9e9ea3' escape is the same value. Both halves need tokens: text.idle for the window labels and, per D7, gtip.hint for the tooltip hint lines, since gtip.muted is .5.

There is no gold wash at .08 (list.hover .10, menu.hover .15, tab.rule .16, list.sel .18). Taking list.hover's rgb with a literal .08 alpha is the 'alpha written at a call site' that #107 forbids, and no reference adopter does it. LootHistory paints list.hover and list.sel unmodified. So list.open is needed. It can be added to the ACCENT_WASH table (SkinDefs.lua:459) at 0.08, which gives every skin a value for free.

No token is translucent white at .55 (icon.tint .7,.7,.72,1; icon.dim .55,.55,.55,1; icon.hot 1,1,1,1; chart.crosshair 1,1,1,.35; chart.marker .8,.8,.8,.6). Any of these changes the chevron's Ka0s Default pixels, and a literal alpha over icon.hot breaks #107. icon.muted is needed.

But skinning-§6 requires a composed BorderGroup to take the composer's own fromSkin companion. OptionsCompose's FROM_SKIN map only knows borderStyle → bar.borderStyle (OptionsCompose.lua:326-333). With it on, the disabled picker's skinValue shows Ka0s Default's 'None' while a solid edge is drawn, and S.Resolve('bar.borderStyle') answers 'None', so a host that obeys Resolve erases the border after R3. A hand-rolled companion beside the composer would break §6/#47. The missing piece is a composer option naming the icon family (fromSkin = 'icon' → an icon border-style token whose Ka0s Default reads 'Solid'/flat). icon.borderSize is optional, since no skin varies icon edge size and R3 can leave the size alone. This recurs in AuraMaster, KickCD and ConsumableMaster, so it is worth solving once in M1.

verdicts.composition: Use two instances from the existing builder (modules/Panel.lua buildFrame, :778-800, which already builds the whole panel from BUILDERS). (1) The STOCK instance is today's code, frame name FRAME_NAME, built as now and never handed to any S.* call, so it is never recorded and no Repaint can touch it. (2) The SKINNED instance is the same buildFrame with a nil or second name, built lazily the first time the choice is not Ka0s Default. It is painted with S.Shell + S.FadeNineSlice/S.FadeRegions (the PortraitFrameTemplate border and header-art clips), S.PageButton(mm,'up'/'down') for min/max, S.Checkbox for the 8 check buttons, S.EditBox for the 3 boxes, S.Dropdown for the 4 WowStyle1 dropdowns, S.Button for the 5 buttons, and S.Text/S.Font for the labels and readout, all from existing SkinDefs tokens. The rule: source 'ka0s' with skin 'ka0s' shows the stock instance and hides the skinned one; any other skin, or the 'eui' source, shows the skinned one. A live switch back to Ka0s Default then replays Ka0s Default tokens onto the hidden skinned twin, which is invisible and harmless, and swaps to the never-painted stock twin. verdicts.reason: Every Ka0s Default token with black RGB was checked (SkinDefs.lua:209-356). The alphas are cover.dim 0.6, bar.bg 0.5, handle.bg 0.75, popup.bg 0.92 and 1 for win.border, menu.border, bar.border and icon.border. None is 0.55 or 0.35. Three generic token-wash routes exist. S.Divider(tex, {token=name}) (SkinPaintExtras.lua:86-101) colors a texture with any named color token. S.Cover and S.Strip go through wash() (:131-163). Each of them answers only the token's full rgba. The two ways to keep today's 0.55 and 0.35 both break anti-pattern #107, which bans an alpha typed at the call site. The first takes cover.dim's RGB and adds a typed alpha. The second paints cover.dim and then calls region SetAlpha(0.55/0.6). Raising either veil to 0.6 changes Ka0s Default, and the two states must stay distinct, so one token cannot serve both. Separately, the dial's veils are textures drawn with Slices.DISC art and tinted by SetVertexColor (Dial_Render.lua:75-82, :498-500). Divider, Cover and Strip call SetColorTexture on a texture target, which would wipe the disc art. So for the wedges, the new tokens must be read with S.Color plus an OnLooksChanged repaint, or LK must add a vertex-tint route. The same shape recurs in ConsumableMaster H5c (black 0.55 shade), so rung 2 applies.

The default of the dial slice highlight (PadStyle.lua:112, dial.slice.highlight with useClassColorHighlight) is a player HUD color. skinning-§6 names only texture, border and font as HUD style that follows the skin. Under ConsumableMaster's D2 precedent it can stay the player's value, with no token needed. That half alone would not be a gap. The pad button's HIGHLIGHT wash is a different case (Pad_Render.lua:207-210). It is not a setting: it is NS.Constants.GOLD plus a typed 0.25, which #107 bans once the addon adopts. No Ka0s Default token holds gold at 0.25. The gold washes are list.hover 0.10, menu.hover 0.15, tab.rule 0.16, list.sel 0.18, section.rule 0.35, handle.edge 0.6, input.focus 0.9 and list.dropLine 0.9 (SkinDefs.lua:263-353). S.Color('text.accent') with a typed 0.25 alpha is a #107 alpha literal. S.ListRow's hover state paints list.hover at 0.10, which changes Ka0s Default. Making the pad wash read the dial's stored highlight would tie it to an unrelated player setting. A player who recolored the dial would see the pad hover change too, and no skin would drive it. So the pad wash needs a token, and hud.hover can also serve as the dial highlight's FROM_SKIN kind.

The icon browser cell is a settings-surface list cell, so S.ListRow(cell, 'selected') is the natural primitive (SkinPaintControls.lua:690-699). It paints list.sel at {1,0.82,0,0.18} and list.selOutline, which is false under Ka0s Default. Today's whole-cell gold 0.7 would become 0.18 with no outline, which changes Ka0s Default. No Ka0s Default token holds gold at 0.7: the nearest are handle.edge 0.6 and input.focus/list.dropLine 0.9. S.Divider(tex, {token=...}) could paint the cell texture only with an exact-value token, and none exists. A typed 0.7 alpha over text.accent's RGB is a #107 alpha literal. Without a new token, the only option is an owner-approved change to Ka0s Default, which the stop rule bars.

Conditional on the owner keeping the ratified 'matches the settings window exactly' look. The relayed owner answer 'keep the ruling' points that way. Since SkinPaint minor 6 (SkinPaint.lua:28-31, FadeRegions and FadeNineSlice at :973-994), Shell, FadeNineSlice and CloseButton fade a stock template's art under every skin, Ka0s Default included. The library has no public give-back. Skin:Untrack only drops the record (Skin.lua:707-713). The give-back inside Track runs only when a frame moves to a second owner. lib:Repaint replays the primitives, which fade again. Three workarounds were checked, and each falls short. __PanelSkinned/SetIgnore(panel) is the player's scope toggle, not a per-skin rule, and it is internal. An addon gate that skips painting while the skin is ka0s copies the EllesmereUI-gate pattern that #107 names. It also cannot undo a live switch from another skin back to Ka0s Default. A reload request exists only for leaving eui (Skin.lua:334-393). Rebuilding the frame from OnLooksChanged leaks frames and is still a gate on the skin key. So only a library option, shared with PG-G1, keeps the template as the client drew it under Ka0s Default while painting it under the other eight skins and eui. If the owner instead accepts the flat look, this stops being a gap: S.Shell plus S.FadeNineSlice plus S.CloseButton cover it, with the Ka0s Default change recorded.
